title: Spain's most famous battle might have been a skirmish.

beats.text: Spain's most famous battle might have been a skirmish.
After 711, only the wild mountains of the north stayed out of Muslim hands. There, a nobleman named Pelayo led a revolt.
A Muslim force marched into a narrow valley at Covadonga to crush him. It was ambushed and beaten.
Later Christian chronicles tell of a holy cave, and a miracle: the attackers' own stones and arrows turning back on them.
But the oldest chronicle of the conquest, written in 754, never mentions Pelayo. Even the year is disputed.
beats.say: But the oldest chronicle of the conquest, written in seven fifty-four, never mentions Pelayo. Even the year is disputed.

beats.text: Whatever happened, Pelayo founded the Kingdom of Asturias. From it grew León, then Castile, and in time, Spain.
Spain calls it the start of the Reconquista. Historians still argue how big it really was. What do you think?
